headline: ServerFault moderator steps down after 15 years amid site decline
summary: After over 15 years of service, a long-time moderator is calling it quits on ServerFault as the Q&A site sees a significant drop in daily questions.
details: A dedicated moderator, who served for over 15 years on Stack Overflow's trilogy sites, has announced their departure from ServerFault. Elected in the first community election in 2011, they are likely among the longest-serving moderators on the platform.

The moderator reflects on the early, more fractious years of ServerFault, citing cultural clashes between international users that necessitated features like post locking and moderator coverage during US night hours.

However, the site has experienced a long-term decline, with question volume dropping significantly since its peak in 2011-2012. Recent months have seen only 2-3 questions posted per day, with the moderator flag queue primarily handling spam.

The moderator also detailed their involvement in combating StackExchange-wide spam campaigns over the past few years, which required real-time manual intervention. While new technical measures have made such attacks more difficult, the experience was taxing.
With the Suggested Edit queue barely active, signaling a slowdown in site activity, the moderator has decided it's time to step down. The community will now decide if a replacement is necessary.

headline_marked: [[Penguin Mail]] launches as open-source Rust email client for Linux with AI
headline: Penguin Mail launches as open-source Rust email client for Linux with AI
summary: This new email client for Linux integrates AI to help manage your inbox, offering features like asking about pending replies or categorizing promotions.
details: Penguin Mail is a new open-source email client built with Rust, designed specifically for Linux users. It aims to provide a more intelligent and efficient way to manage your inbox.
The client features an AI assistant that can understand natural language queries. Users can ask questions like 'which sent mail is still waiting on a reply?' or 'what is in my promotions folder?'
Penguin Mail accesses your mailboxes using the app's own tools, ensuring privacy and control over your data. It then presents the information based on the AI assistant's analysis.
Beyond email, Penguin Mail also includes calendar functionality and supports Gmail and any IMAP account. It's designed to run on your own computer, offering a self-hosted solution.
The project is available on GitHub, inviting contributions from the open-source community to further develop its features and capabilities.
caption:
Meet Penguin Mail: the open-source Linux email client with an AI assistant that understands your inbox.

Penguin Mail is a new open-source email client built with Rust, designed specifically for Linux users. It aims to provide a more intelligent and efficient way to manage your inbox.

The client features an AI assistant that can understand natural language queries. Users can ask questions like 'which sent mail is still waiting on a reply?' or 'what is in my promotions folder?'

Penguin Mail accesses your mailboxes using the app's own tools, ensuring privacy and control over your data. It then presents the information based on the AI assistant's analysis.

Beyond email, Penguin Mail also includes calendar functionality and supports Gmail and any IMAP account. It's designed to run on your own computer, offering a self-hosted solution.

The project is available on GitHub, inviting contributions from the open-source community to further develop its features and capabilities.
